identity.title: Detection of Lensing Substructure Using ALMA Observations of the Dusty Galaxy SDP.81

paper_type_evidence.quote: We apply our formalism to ALMA observations of SDP.81. We find evidence for the presence of a $M=10^{8.96\pm 0.12} M_{\odot}$ subhalo near one of the images

question.value: How abundant is dark matter substructure near the lens galaxy of SDP.81, measured by fitting ALMA visibilities, and is it consistent with LCDM?

evidence.quote: We study the abundance of substructure in the matter density near galaxies using ALMA Science Verification observations of the strong lensing system SDP.81.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00016.SV.
We used only the calibrated continuum data from bands 6 and 7.
For ALMA long-baseline campaign observations of SDP.81 (cite: Fomalont:15), visibilities were typically recorded every 0.5 seconds
We use the recent ALMA Science Verification observations of the strongly lensed system SDP.81 (cite: SDP81)

provided.value: Image of the lensing galaxy shown against the ALMA arcs

evidence.quote: Figure [4](#fig:SDP81ALMAHST) shows the lensing galaxy observed by the *Hubble Space Telescope* (greyscale) superimposed on the lensed arcs observed by ALMA.

provided.value: Lens galaxy r-band magnitude and environment (RedMaPPer cluster membership)

evidence.quote: which is $M_r = -21.88 \pm 0.015$ using the SDSS DR10 magnitudes

what.value: RedMaPPer cluster catalog membership and mass-richness relation for the SDP.81 environment

evidence.quote: Assuming the mass–richness relationship of (cite: Rykoff:14), this corresponds to a mass of $\sim 2.6\times 10^{14} M_{\odot}$.

what.value: AGES luminosity function used for abundance matching

evidence.quote: we assume the AGES luminosity function (cite: Kochanek:12)

evidence.quote: the lensed images were used to simulate ALMA observations using the Common Astronomy Software Applications package (CASA).

evidence.quote: ($4096^3$ particles in a $400~\text{Mpc}/h$ box, `ds14_i`) from the Dark Sky Simulations (cite: Skillman:14)

evidence.quote: We used only the calibrated continuum data from bands 6 and 7.

what.value: Subhalo modeled as a pseudo-Jaffe profile, following the earlier proposal for ALMA substructure detection

evidence.quote: We follow (cite: Hezaveh13A) and model the subhalo deflection field using a truncated isothermal surface density profile

what.value: Pixelated source framework and Bayesian evidence normalization of source prior

evidence.quote: The general framework of fitting strongly lensed images with pixelated sources is described in detail in (cite: warren:03) and (cite: suyu:06).

what.value: Subhalo mass function model and calibration methodology

evidence.quote: we follow the methodology presented in (cite: Mao:15)

what.value: MCMC sampler of Goodman and Weare, implemented following emcee

evidence.quote: we have implemented the Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithm proposed by (cite: mcmchammer). We follow the procedure described in (cite: emcee).

method.value: Bin visibilities sharing a baseline within a short time into uv cells; estimate noise from differences of visibilities that null the sky, scaling Tsys

evidence.quote: We estimate the noise variance for each visibility using the procedure described above and bin the visibilities in 12 meter cells.

key_parameters.value: 12 m cells; bins within ≲20 min on the same baseline; ~0.5 million binned visibilities from ~10 million

evidence.quote: This results in $\sim0.5$ million binned visibilities, a factor of $\sim 20$ fewer than the original $\sim10$ million.

key_parameters.value: Retain binned visibilities with noise below 5.0 mJy (band 6) and 5.5 mJy (band 7)

evidence.quote: We, therefore, decide to model binned visibilities with noise lower than 5.0 and 5.5 mJy in bands 6 and 7 respectively

assumptions.value: Noise rms proportional to Tsys; variance of differenced visibilities equals twice noise variance

evidence.quote: we can simply assume that the variance in the subtracted visibilities is equal to twice the noise variance

validation.value: Both noise methods give consistent results

evidence.quote: We try both methods and find that they provide consistent results.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit smooth lens model to visibilities

method.value: Fit visibilities with a pixelated source, analytic marginalization over source pixels, antenna phase errors per baseline and time, and MCMC over lens parameters; initial localization with baselines <2 km

evidence.quote: We first use only the subset of baselines shorter than 2 km in our initial MCMC analysis to localize the neighborhood of the best fit.

key_parameters.value: Singular elliptical power law plus m=3,4 multipoles plus external shear; 12 free parameters

evidence.quote: Overall, therefore, our primary lens model contains 12 freely adjustable parameters.
we assume a flat $\Lambda$CDM expansion history with mean matter density $\Omega_M = 0.267$ and current expansion rate $H_0 = 71$ km Mpc$^{-1}$ s$^{-1}$.
we set ${\bf C}_\eta^{-1} = 0$, i.e., we assume no prior on the lens model parameters.

fitting.value: Gaussian likelihood with Gaussian source prior; MCMC after Goodman and Weare, following emcee

evidence.quote: We follow the procedure described in (cite: emcee).

validation.value: Tested on mock ALMA data; parameters recovered without bias with gradient and curvature priors

evidence.quote: in both cases we successfully manage to recover the parameters with no apparent biases.

method.value: Map Delta E, twice the marginalized log-posterior difference, over subhalo position and mass using a linear approximation about the smooth model, marginalizing over lens, source and phase parameters

evidence.quote: We search for subhalos over a range of subhalo masses, over a $8\times8$ arcsec area around the lens center.

key_parameters.value: Pseudo-Jaffe subhalo with r_t = (sigma_v/(sqrt2 sigma_G)) r_E; initial search at M=10^8.6 Msun

evidence.quote: we assume that $r_t$ is related to $\sigma_v$ by $r_t = (\sigma_v/\sqrt{2}\sigma_G)r_{\rm E}$

validation.value: Bands 6 and 7 analyzed separately give a consistent pattern; alternative literature lens models give similar results

evidence.quote: Our analysis reveals a consistent pattern between the two bands (see Figure [5](#initial_search))

analysis_steps.goal: Nonlinear fit with subhalo and MCMC

method.value: Add a subhalo with 3 parameters (mass, 2-D position), refit jointly in bands 6 and 7 fully nonlinearly, then sample with MCMC

evidence.quote: we then expanded our lens model to include a subhalo, with 3 adjustable parameters: mass $M_{\rm sub}$, and 2-D location $\bm{x}_{\rm sub}$.

fitting.value: MCMC over smooth lens and subhalo parameters; 68% uncertainties

evidence.quote: Best-fit lens parameters with 68% uncertainties

validation.value: No significant degeneracy between subhalo and smooth lens parameters including multipoles

evidence.quote: We do not find evidence for significant degeneracies between the subhalo parameters and the parameters of the smooth lens model

method.value: Repeat the linearized search about the model including the detected subhalo; nonlinear fit of a second subhalo

evidence.quote: We repeated our search for a second subhalo, by linearly expanding about a smooth model now containing a subhalo of mass $M_{\rm sub}=10^{8.96} M_{\odot}$.

validation.value: Second object marginal (<5 sigma) and possibly a modeling artifact, so not claimed as detection

evidence.quote: First, the detection is marginal $(<5\sigma)$.

method.value: Combine Poisson likelihood from detected subhalos with exclusion areas from Delta E maps, assuming linear addition of Delta E; fit dn/dlogM = A (M/Mpivot)^-eta

evidence.loc: 5.3 Bounds on the subhalo mass function
evidence.quote: We describe the mass function using a simple parametrization, $dn/d\log M = A\,(M/M_{\rm pivot})^{-\eta}$

assumptions.value: Poisson process with spatially uniform mean projected density; subhalo effects add linearly

evidence.loc: 5.3 Bounds on the subhalo mass function
evidence.quote: We assume that the incidence of subhalos is a Poisson process with mean projected number density $n(M)$ that is spatially uniform

validation.value: Linear addition tends to underestimate decrease in posterior for overlapping subhalos, so bounds slightly conservative

evidence.loc: 5.3 Bounds on the subhalo mass function
evidence.quote: suggesting that our bounds below are (slightly) conservative.

method.value: Predict projected subhalo mass function from calibrated M0(Mhost, chost) relation with NFW radial distribution, marginalizing over host mass and concentration from abundance matching

evidence.quote: we treat it as a free parameter, along with other parameters describing the lens halo: the host halo mass and concentration ($M_\text{host}$, $c_\text{host}$), and the log–log slope ($\eta$)

key_parameters.value: eta=0.9; c_subs/c_host = 0.2 and 1.0; abundance matching with 0.2 dex scatter

evidence.quote: we assume the mass function slope is $\eta=0.9$, and we show two possible values for the subhalo concentration, $c_\text{subs}/c_\text{host}=0.2$ and 1.0

assumptions.value: Subhalo spatial distribution independent of mass, isotropic, NFW radial profile

evidence.quote: the subhalo spatial distribution is *independent* from the subhalo mass function

validation.value: Limits consistent with theory but parameters degenerate

evidence.quote: substructure limits from SDP.81 are currently consistent with theoretical predictions.
the lensed images were used to simulate ALMA observations using the Common Astronomy Software Applications package (CASA).

used_for.value: Distributed dense linear algebra for the Fourier operator

evidence.quote: we take advantage of the “*Elemental*” dense linear algebra library, which efficiently performs linear algebra operations over distributed cores

used_for.value: MCMC sampling procedure, parallelized with MPI

evidence.quote: Our implementation allows sampling the posterior in parallel, over many cores, taking advantage of the MPI message-passing system.
$\log_{10} (M_{\rm sub})$ | subhalo mass ($M_\odot$) | $8.96 \pm 0.12$
with a significance of $6.9\sigma$ in a joint fit to data from bands 6 and 7

evidence.quote: improves the marginalized log posterior fit by $\Delta\ensuremath{{\cal  E} }= -47.3$ in the joint fit
$x_{\rm sub}$ | subhalo position x ($^{\prime\prime}$) | $-0.694 \pm 0.025$
$\alpha$ | radial slope | $1.06  \pm 0.03$

results_numeric.quantity: Delta E for second subhalo (~1e8 Msun)

evidence.quote: could improve the fit marginally, with $\Delta\ensuremath{{\cal  E} }\approx -22$, compared to the 1-subhalo model.

results_numeric.quantity: 95% central range of n at 1e9 Msun

evidence.loc: 5.3 Bounds on the subhalo mass function
evidence.quote: the central 95% confidence region is $0.012\ {\rm arcsec}^{-2} < n < 0.2\ {\rm arcsec}^{-2}$

results_numeric.quantity: Chi-squared of smooth fit over 5x5 arcsec region

evidence.quote: our model obtains $\chi^2 = 2\times 10^5$ for $1.7\times 10^5$ degrees of freedom

results_numeric.quantity: Lens host halo mass from abundance matching

evidence.quote: The typical halo mass we found with this procedure is roughly $8.7 \times 10^{12} M_\odot h^{-1}$, with an approximate uncertainty of a factor of 3.5.

findings_qualitative.value: Sensitivity to individual subhalos is lost at masses below ~1e7 Msun

evidence.quote: the SDP.81 data set loses sensitivity for detecting individual subhalos at masses $\lesssim 10^7 M_\odot$.

findings_qualitative.value: Marginalizing over antenna phase errors removes false positives that appear in uncorrected mock analyses

evidence.quote: when phase errors are marginalized over appropriately, resulting in the disappearance of the false detections.

claims.hypothesis: Does ALMA visibility data of SDP.81 reveal a dark matter subhalo?
claims.experiment: Linearized search then nonlinear fit of bands 6 and 7 continuum visibilities
claims.result: Subhalo of log M = 8.96±0.12 with Delta E = -47.3, 6.9 sigma, seen in both bands
claims.finding: A subhalo is detected in projected mass

evidence.quote: detects a $M=10^{8.96\pm 0.12} M_{\odot}$ subhalo with a significance of $6.9\sigma$

claims.experiment: Second linearized search about model with one subhalo
claims.result: ~1e8 Msun candidate with Delta E ≈ -22, <5 sigma, near the first subhalo

evidence.quote: we do not label the second object as a detection, however we do include it in our main lens model.

claims.hypothesis: Is the measured substructure abundance consistent with LCDM?
claims.experiment: Compare constraints with predicted subhalo mass function including host halo uncertainties
claims.result: Limits consistent with predictions, possibly hinting lower normalization
claims.finding: Consistent given current host halo uncertainties

evidence.quote: substructure limits from SDP.81 are currently consistent with theoretical predictions.

claims.hypothesis: Should substructure analyses use visibilities rather than CLEAN images?
claims.experiment: Mock tests with and without phase error marginalization
claims.result: Uncorrected phase errors give numerous false positives
claims.finding: Visibility modeling with marginalization is needed; may explain disagreement with Inoue et al.

evidence.quote: we recommend that substructure analyses operate on the visibilities

why_this_method.value: Visibility-domain modeling allows marginalizing antenna phase errors and has well-characterized noise, unlike CLEAN images

evidence.quote: In addition, CLEAN images are produced through a non-linear deconvolution procedure whose effects on the data and the correlated noise properties can not be well quantified.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Gradient and curvature source priors compared on mock data; DC mode removed from the clump power-spectrum prior to avoid magnification bias

evidence.quote: To fix this issue, we removed the DC mode from this covariance matrix

limitations_admitted.value: Simple spherical pseudo-Jaffe subhalo profile may leave residuals fitted by lower-mass substructure

evidence.quote: We have assumed an extremely simple mass profile for the subhalos, a spherical tidally truncated pseudo-Jaffe model

limitations_admitted.value: Only continuum used; CO line data not analyzed; weaker data corruptions such as decorrelation not studied

evidence.quote: The effects of decorrelation, visibility smearing due to frequency averaging, choice of parameterization for antenna phase error corrections, and antenna amplitude errors are among these effects.

referee_caveats_inferred: Only ~40% of visibilities used, selected by noise cut; effect on result not tested
Result depends on pseudo-Jaffe profile and fixed truncation relation
Significance from Laplace/linearized Delta E; no independent validation on real data
Host halo mass and subhalo concentration degenerate, limiting LCDM test
Detection near a cluster member may be affected by environment

data_public_as_stated.value: ALMA Science Verification data, cited and acknowledged

evidence.quote: This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2011.0.00016.SV.

missing_for_reproduction: Source prior choice and grid for SDP.81

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens to hundreds of GB for SV continuum visibilities of bands 6 and 7; heavy compute needed
reproducibility.score_reason: Public data and clear formalism, but bespoke code, missing sampler and prior details, and cluster-scale compute make exact reproduction hard.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Data are public but the recipe needs a custom visibility-domain lens pipeline with incomplete settings.
